Which PTFE product form do you need?

If you need…Start withWhy
Flange gaskets, washers, liners or slide padsPTFE sheet or cut gasketsFlat parts are cut from moulded or skived sheet.
Turned parts — valve seats, spacers, bushesPTFE rodRod is the most economical stock for round machined parts.
Corrosive fluid transfer, sleeving or instrument linesPTFE tube or pipeInert bore with a wide temperature range.
Dry-running, low-friction bearingsPTFE bushesSelf-lubricating; filled grades carry more load.
Seals for aggressive media or extreme temperaturePTFE seals & O-ringsWorks where elastomers swell or harden.
A part made to your drawingCustom machiningWe select the stock and machine the finished part.

PTFE grades we work with

Every product form is available in virgin PTFE, and most in filled grades. Fillers change how PTFE behaves under load, wear and heat — a quick comparison:

General guidance from published data. Filler percentages vary between compounds — confirm the exact grade for your application. *Ask for compliance documentation for food or pharma contact before ordering.
GradeWhat it changesWatch-outsTypical uses
Virgin PTFEHighest purity; best chemical resistance and electrical insulationLowest compressive strength; most prone to creep (cold flow)Chemical service, electrical insulation, food and pharma contact parts*
Glass-filled
commonly 15–25 %		Better compressive strength and wear resistance; less creepAbrasive to soft mating surfaces; glass is attacked by hydrofluoric acid and hot strong alkalisValve seats, seals, gaskets, structural pads
Carbon-filled
often ~25 %, may include graphite		High compressive strength and wear resistance; better thermal conductivity; antistaticNot an electrical insulatorPiston rings, seals and bearings in water, steam and dry gas
Bronze-filled
commonly 40–60 %		Best creep and wear resistance; highest thermal conductivityReduced chemical resistance (acids, ammonia); electrically conductiveHydraulic seals and guide rings, bearings, wear strips
Graphite-filled
commonly 5–15 %		Lower friction and good dry-running behaviourLower strength than carbon- or bronze-filledBushes and seals running against softer shafts

For a deeper comparison, read virgin vs filled PTFE.

PTFE turling and granules

Machining PTFE produces clean turnings (turling). We supply PTFE turling and granules in bulk for reprocessing, resin blending, powder sintering and filler compounding. Material can be sorted by grade — virgin turnings are kept separate from filled grades.

  • Virgin turning scrap
  • Mixed filled turnings
  • Granulated PTFE
  • Bulk packing
  • Sorted by grade
  • Granule size on request

Send the grade, quantity and intended use, and we will confirm what is available.

Ask Our Team

Common Questions

PTFE Product FAQs

Ask a Question

Teflon™ is a trademark of The Chemours Company for its fluoropolymer products, including PTFE. In everyday industrial use “Teflon sheet” or “Teflon rod” usually means PTFE. We manufacture and supply PTFE products; we do not sell the branded product.

Yes — sheets, rods and tubes as stock or cut to size, and finished gaskets, seals, bushes and machined components made to your drawing.

Virgin PTFE gives the best chemical resistance and electrical insulation. Choose a filled grade when the part carries load, wears against another surface or must resist creep. Share the application and we will recommend a grade.

Yes. We supply PTFE turnings and granules in bulk, sorted by grade, for reprocessing and compounding.
